name: Gurubashi Arena
summary: In southern Stranglethorn Vale, pirates and wandering brawlers gather at Gurubashi Arena. Fighters clash over locked chests of treasure in its ancient stone ring.

sections.title: A Legacy of Blood
sections.body: Before humans or orcs came to Stranglethorn Vale, the Gurubashi troll empire raised the Gurubashi Arena, also called the Great Arena. It honored their martial strength. In ancient days, champions fought to the death on its sands, until troll blood slicked the earth.

sections.title: The Booty Run
sections.body:
The Gurubashi Empire has fractured into warring tribes, yet bloodshed still comes to the arena floor. Now lawless buccaneers and ruffians gather for another spectacle. Short John Mithril, a pirate, oversees the grounds.

Every few hours, a chest of plundered booty is hauled to the ring's center. Anyone who steps onto the floor becomes fair game. Faction allegiances fall away, and every combatant must fight all comers to reach the prize.

faq.answer: The Gurubashi Empire built the arena centuries ago, while it ruled the southern regions of the Eastern Kingdoms. The enormous stadium hosted lethal combat trials and ancient troll rituals honoring the loa.

faq.q: Why do people fight here now?
faq.answer: Local pirates use the arena for illicit entertainment. Every few hours, a pirate captain brings a treasure chest to the center of the sands, and anyone who dares enter the ring can fight to claim it.
Short John Mithril is the pirate who oversees the arena and its regular chest deliveries. He rewards combatants who survive the brawls and recover his arena treasures.

faq.q: Why can members of my own faction attack me here?
aliases: why is gurubashi free for all
faq.answer: Once you cross onto the arena sands, faction treaties and military alliances are suspended. Only those fighting alongside you in your immediate battle party are spared your blade.

angles.text: As a troll, you walk sacred ground, a monument to the old Gurubashi Empire. Champions once shed blood on these sands.
As a warrior, you face a test of martial skill on these sands. Grand war politics fall away, and personal grit and survival decide the fight.
